steps: Command receives one stable operation identity.
Authoritative store commits and records replication intent.
Secondary write applies idempotently using the same identity.
Any partial failure is retained and retried or reconciled.

lesson.scenario: A customer-profile migration writes old and new stores while exposing partial failure for deterministic repair.

steps.title: Canonicalize the intent
steps.narration: The API computes canonical payload checksum sha256:7a91 and commits schema v3 version 18 to the authoritative SQL store.

steps.outcome: The source has one durable versioned update.
steps.invariant: Partial success is recorded durably, repair is version-guarded and idempotent, and one store remains explicitly authoritative during migration.

steps.title: Attempt the target write
steps.narration: The v4 document write times out after 200 ms, leaving its outcome unknown.

steps.title: Persist repair evidence
steps.narration: The repair record includes source version, target schema v4, checksum 7a91, and operation ID prof-881.

steps.outcome: The divergence is durable and observable.

steps.title: Repair idempotently
steps.narration: The worker reads the source, transforms v3 to v4, and conditionally upserts only when target version is below 18.

check.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: A retry cannot overwrite a newer target value.
steps.invariant: Partial success is recorded durably, repair is version-guarded and idempotent, and one store remains explicitly authoritative during migration.

steps.title: Verify convergence
steps.narration: The reconciler compares normalized fields and checksum 7a91 at version 18 in both stores.
steps.outcome: The repaired record is proven equivalent.
steps.invariant: Partial success is recorded durably, repair is version-guarded and idempotent, and one store remains explicitly authoritative during migration.
